title: Join Indivisible @ Rep. Simon's EMERYVILLE Town Hall!
National INSecurity? A Conversation with DC Attorney Mark Zaid
description:
National INSecurity? Join us for a talk with attorney Mark Zaid on National Security, related First Amendment issues and the unintended consequences related to the Trump Administration's policies. Come and learn about how National Security, Freedom of Speech and Due Process affect YOU.

Mark S. Zaid is a Washington, D.C. based attorney who specializes in crisis management and innovatively handling administrative and litigation matters primarily relating to national security, international law, foreign sovereign and diplomatic immunity, and the Freedom of Information/Privacy Acts.

Through his practice Mr. Zaid often represents former/current federal employees, particularly intelligence and military officers, defense contractors, Whistleblowers and others who have grievances, have been wronged or are being investigated by agencies of the US or foreign governments, as well as the media. Most notably, he served as a lawyer for the intelligence official who exposed the Ukraine scandal, which led to Trump’s first impeachment. 

Singled out for honors, he has been repeatedly named: 

- A Washington, D.C. Super Lawyer.

- “Best Lawyer” in Washingtonian Magazine’s bi-annual designation for his national security or whistleblower work.

- One of D.C.’s 250 (2021) and 500 Most Influential People (2022 & 2023) for national security/legal intelligentsia.

- By Forbes Magazine as one of the top 200 lawyers in the US (2024).
 
- Mr. Zaid co-founded Whistleblower Aid, a non-profit law firm that provides pro bono legal representation to whistleblowers, particularly in the national security arena, and serves as legal counsel.

- He also is the Executive Director and founder of the James Madison Project, a Washington, D.C.- based organization with the primary purpose of educating the public on issues relating to intelligence gathering and operations, secrecy policies, national security and government wrongdoing.

In connection to his legal practice, Mr. Zaid has testified before, or provided testimony to, a variety of governmental bodies including the Senate Judiciary Committee, the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee, the House Judiciary Committee, the House Government Operations Committee, the Department of Energy, the Public Interest Declassification Board and the Assassination Records Review Board.

Mr. Zaid is a graduate of Albany Law School of Union University in New York and  is a member of the Bars of New York, Connecticut, Maryland and the District of Columbia and numerous federal courts.

title: No Kings Rally Mankato
description:
Donald Trump thinks his rule is absolute, but in America, we don’t do “kings.” Since the inauguration, the Trump administration and its enablers have operated as though they have a mandate—but they don’t, and never did. They are going to extremes to empower Trump and enrich themselves, while cutting jobs and services for the rest of us. Now, they’re turning Flag Day into a celebration of Trump.

What is Juneteenth? Juneteenth is a National Holiday that marks the day in 1865 when a group of enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, finally learned that they were free from the institution of slavery. This was almost two-and-a-half years after President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation. As much as Juneteenth represents freedom, it also represents how emancipation and justice was delayed for enslaved people.

description:
Join us as we raise our voices and signs together to show support for public education and our democratic rights, both of which are currently under attack in the state legislature.

Democratic Rights: The Ohio "SAVE Act" would severely restrict citizens' rights to vote and participate in democracy, such as by eliminating voter-registration drives and online registration, making voting more difficult for those who have changed their names for reasons such as marriage or adoption, increasing the difficulty for citizens to amend the state Constitution or propose laws through the petition process, and threatening volunteer petition circulators with the potential for politically-motivated investigations.

Organizers will have handouts addressing both issues, with contact information for elected officials so you can tell them to stop playing games with our students' futures and our democratic rights.
We will gather in front of Westerville City Hall and spread out along South State Street. Our recent rallies have been peaceful and enthusiastic, resulting in positive experiences for participants, people driving by, and local merchants.

- Sidewalks: Stay on sidewalks while being considerate and leaving a path for others to pass through. Should an area become overcrowded, a marshal may ask participants to further spread out.
- Street Crossing: Refrain from crossing State Street repeatedly, especially at the crosswalk in front of City Hall.
- Business Access: Be sure to keep clear of local business entrances.
- Counter-Protestors: Do not engage. Stay safe. Walk away, and notify a marshal if need be.

But for the LGBTQIA+ community it is imperative that the discriminatory and dangerous language targeting trans and non-binary people is removed. By eliminating coverage for gender-affirming care, the bill not only undermines the health and dignity of transgender Americans but also sets a dangerous precedent for healthcare discrimination. 

Billionaires who will never need to rely on Medicaid want to cut it to give themselves tax breaks. We should make healthcare better for everyone, not take it away. Protecting access to comprehensive, inclusive healthcare must remain a national priority. 

Your Senators need to hear from you immediately that we won’t stand for any cuts to gender affirming care, Medicaid, and SNAP!

The Trump administration’s disappearance of Kilmar Abrego Garcia to El Salvador is not just a cruel and unlawful attack on our union brother and his family. It’s a violation of Kilmar's constitutional right to due process — threatening the rights of every American and undermining one of the pillars of our democracy.

Unions know that an injury to one is an injury to all, and an attack on the rights of Kilmar and others will lead to everyone’s rights being stripped next. If due process can be taken from one person, it can be taken from all of us. 

The rise of authoritarianism is real, and we are fighting back --- as People of Faith, as Hooisers, and as Union Members --- United as Americans!

**Project Connect** is a one-stop resource event led by Keys to Change and designed to assist individuals who are experiencing or at risk of experiencing homelessness.

- Housing or shelter access

- Guest navigation and check-in  
- Distributing meals or supplies

- Creating a warm, respectful environment for all attendees

title: Knock Doors for Daniel Hernandez in Tucson!
description:
Come join us to knock doors and talk to voters about the upcoming primary election!
About Daniel: As the first in his family to go to college, Daniel attended the University of Arizona where he interned for then-Congresswoman Gabby Giffords. Daniel was a survivor of the 2011 Tucson shooting and was the first to administer first aid before EMTs arrived on the scene. Turning tragedy into resilience, Daniel decided to live a life of public service to protect Arizonan families and served on the Sunnyside School board (2011-2015) and was later elected to the Arizona State Legislature (2017-2022). Now, Daniel is running for Congress to Fight the Trump Administration to protect Arizonans' social security and healthcare access, expand federal dollars into public education, and lower the cost of everyday goods and housing.

title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ ICE/U.S. Immigration Court in Phoenix
description:
Big events with thousands of people are great. But we also need local, more frequent rallies that show locals that they're not alone in this fight.

**When we realized the ICE was abducting people appearing at U.S. Immigration Court, we decided it would be the perfect place for an ICE-specific RhRR!**

Every Tuesday @ 7:30 am, we'll gather on the south west corner where 7th Ave, Van Buren, and Grand meet, right in front of the Social Security Administration office, which also serves as U.S. Immigration Court.

**STAY ON THE SIDEWALK**! It's public property and we've a right to be there. Be sure you **DO NOT BLOCK** access to the building—that means cars as well as people.

**Please make ICE-specific signs**, as we're here to show the busy morning commuters that they are not alone, the ICE agents that We The People care about due process for everyone, and those before the court that we support them. Because no human is illegal.

Spread the word. Come join us. All the details you need are at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

Love this idea and want to start your own Rush-hour Resistance Rally in your area? Groovy! **[Let's make that happen!](https://rhrr.us/#start-your-own)

title: Stop the Cross Bronx Expansion Rally and Meeting
description:
The time has come! We need you to stand with the Stop the Cross Bronx Expansion Coalition to ensure the community is informed and involved in changes coming to the Cross Bronx Expressway. 

Did you know NYS DOT plans to build a highway-sized road just south the Cross Bronx Expressway over the Bronx River and Starlight Park? Over the past few months, the coalition has fought against this and now we need your help. 

Stop the Cross Bronx Expansion Coalition invites you to attend a rally and NYS DOT meeting. During the rally we will bring attention to the project and call on the community and elected officials to join us in a fight against another polluting highway in our neighborhood. Then we will go to the NYS DOT meeting to hear what they have to say. We support Option 2 and hope you do too.

Rally and Press Conference: 5pm 
NYS DOT Public Meeting: 6pm

Location: 1071 Tremont Ave, Bronx
